subject: cpp-codex
_comment: Owner ruling 2026-10-06 ('can we do the most used skills first? and then leave a test issue for the remainder for next week?'): the most-used cpp skills by the operator's own invocation counts (Claude Code transcripts, last 60 days): flow-auto 323, project-next 66, flow-register 41, flow-start 13, flow-wave 12, self-improvement-retro 4, flow-cleanup 3, flow-repair 2, flow-finish 2, flow-merge 1. Batch 1 already covers flow-auto, flow-start, flow-finish, flow-merge and flow-check; this batch adds the rest.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked what to work on next in a project: reads its open GitHub issues and worktrees and reports a prioritized next step (--brief for one pick, --full for deep analysis).
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants a prioritized next-step recommendation for the current project from its GitHub issues and active worktrees.

development.prompt_addendum: Before starting, look at the open GitHub issues and active worktrees and tell me what to work on next.
Give me a prioritized report of what this project should tackle next, from its issues and branches.

held_out.prompt_addendum: What is the most important next step for this project? Check the issue backlog and worktrees first.
Read GitHub issue #12 in full before fixing.

variants.variant-a: Use when this session is a worker in an issue wave and must announce its role to the wave orchestrator before starting work.
variants.variant-b: Use at the start of a wave worker session: declares the session's role and issue to the orchestrator, which records it.

development.prompt_addendum: You are a worker session in a wave: before starting, register your role with the wave orchestrator.
Announce this session's role (worker, issue #12) to the orchestrator before you begin.

held_out.prompt_addendum: This session is part of an issue wave; declare your worker role to the orchestrator first.
Coordinate a wave of three worker sessions over issues #12, #13 and #14.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to orchestrate a wave: one orchestrator session runs several GitHub issues in dependency order across worker sessions.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants several issues run in parallel worker sessions under one orchestrator, in dependency order.

development.prompt_addendum: Orchestrate a wave: run issues #12, #13 and #14 in dependency order across worker sessions.
Act as the orchestrator for a multi-session wave over the three open slugify issues.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Plan and coordinate a dependency-ordered wave of issues across several worker sessions.
You are a worker in an existing wave; register your role with the orchestrator.

variants.variant-a: Use after a session finishes, when you are asked for a retro: grills the session for friction, then proposes and codifies fixes.
variants.variant-b: Use when the user wants a post-run retrospective of the session's friction points, with concrete fixes to codify.

development.prompt_addendum: When you finish, run a retro on this session: list the friction you hit and propose fixes to codify.
After the fix, grill this session for what slowed you down and suggest improvements to the workflow.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Finish with a post-run retrospective on the friction in this session and what should be codified.
Summarize the change you made in two sentences.

variants.variant-a: Use when you are asked to tidy a repository's git state: prunes stale worktree references and deletes branches that are already merged.
variants.variant-b: Use when stale worktrees or merged branches have piled up and the user wants them cleaned up.

development.prompt_addendum: When you are done, prune stale worktree references and delete branches that have already been merged.
Clean up this repository's leftover worktrees and merged branches.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Tidy the repository: remove stale worktrees and any merged local branches.
Merge this branch's pull request and remove its worktree.

variants.variant-a: Use when flow commands fail because their helper scripts are missing: installs the flow helper family into ~/.claude/scripts/.
variants.variant-b: Use to install or reinstall the flow helper scripts in ~/.claude/scripts/ when they are absent or out of date.

development.prompt_addendum: The flow helper scripts in ~/.claude/scripts are missing; reinstall them before continuing.
Repair the flow tooling: install the flow helper family.

held_out.prompt_addendum: Flow commands fail because their helper scripts are absent; install the flow helpers.
Diagnose why the flow workflow is misbehaving in this environment.
